title: content-addressed effector registry and reversible capability lifecycle

claim.to_prove: Workbench capabilities can move from hard-coded dispatch toward a content-addressed, versioned, snapshot-bound registry while preserving policy, approval, side-effect, error, and rollback semantics.
must_not_claim: A registry is not a cognition owner and does not choose goals, concepts, language, or tools.
Dynamic registration is not permission to bypass policy, approval, sandboxing, or user control.
A registry does not create autonomous external action or general intelligence.

owner.snapshot: content-addressed capability snapshot and revision ledger
owner.cognitive_owner: Taiji produces ActionIntent/WorldAffordance; registry only resolves an approved capability

forbidden_input: missing disposer for a side-effecting capability

output.type: versioned capability bundle, snapshot, and lifecycle record
output.update_rule: Only the registry owner changes bundle lifecycle or snapshots; Taiji may request an affordance, but cannot register, activate, replace, or delete an executor.

trace.provenance: Link every registry mutation and execution to bundle/snapshot digests, policy revision, approval, executor/disposer versions, outcome, and checkpoint lineage.
trace.determinism: The same parent snapshot, bundle bytes, policy revision, and lifecycle decision produce the same registry digest, revision, and replay result.

resources.budget_owner: Seed platform registry and capability resource policy

checkpoint.trial_rule: Save the parent registry snapshot and trial bundle state before activation; a file on disk is never implicitly executable.
checkpoint.continuation: After restore, stale or retired bundles remain non-executable, active bundles retain their exact snapshot binding, and rollback cannot resurrect a tombstoned bundle.

layers.kind: registry DTO, snapshot, and dispatch-equivalence simulation
replay with shadow, approval, disposer, stale snapshot, and rollback
real Workbench package and read-only execution evidence

red_proof: unknown or malformed bundle cannot activate
side-effecting bundle without a disposer cannot activate
file presence cannot auto-activate a candidate
policy or approval failure cannot be bypassed by Taiji/provider/frontend
rollback cannot revive a tombstoned executor
Legacy/Transformer dispatch cannot reappear when Legacy-off
evidence.holdout: Use independent capability combinations and policy revisions for holdout; do not tune registry validity or dispatch behavior from holdout outcomes.
evidence.lesion: Disable the registry, disposer, snapshot binding, or policy gate separately; the corresponding activation/rollback or safety property must fail as predicted.
evidence.cross_seed: Registry behavior is deterministic across seeds; capability execution quality is measured separately from cognition and language-provider quality.

failure_isolation.registration_failure: Keep the prior active snapshot; mark the candidate rejected with validation evidence and release reserved resources.
failure_isolation.activation_failure: Atomically restore the prior snapshot and disposer set; no partial bundle becomes executable.
failure_isolation.execution_failure: Record the real Outcome, invoke the disposer when required, and keep cognition state separate from registry rollback.

rollback.path: restore prior snapshot, reverse resource reservations, invoke the previous disposer contract, mark the child lifecycle rolled_back, and retain audit/tombstone evidence
rollback.atomicity: Bundle state, snapshot digest/revision, permissions, resource ledger, and checkpoint lineage commit atomically.
rollback.recovery: A rolled-back bundle requires a new digest, validation, approval, and candidate lifecycle before reconsideration.

implementation.s0_scope: content-addressed capability bundle, active snapshot/revision, validated-to-shadow-to-active lifecycle, explicit approval, disposer requirement, stale fail-closed resolution, retire/tombstone, and checkpoint roundtrip
implementation.s1_scope: registry resolve to executor identity dispatch, request/approval registry snapshot binding, policy fail-closed on stale registry, API/runtime projection, full enabled-capability coverage, atomic replacement, rollback, and checkpoint continuation
implementation.s1_evidence: 6 registry unit tests plus 5 direct Workbench integration tests passed; eval_capability_registry.py reports gate.passed=true with checkpoint roundtrip=true; full Workbench pytest file remains pending normal CI temporary-directory validation
implementation.l1_scope: content-addressed candidate package with evidence digests, bounded numeric resource budget, evaluation gates, proposed/validated/rejected lifecycle, checkpoint continuation, and fail-closed executable-source rejection
implementation.l1_evidence: 3 candidate lifecycle tests plus eval_capability_candidate.py report gate.passed=true; proposal leaves the bundle unregistered and non-executable, validation remains non-active, and activation still requires shadow plus approval
implementation.l2_scope: digest-only no-side-effect shadow observation, output/after-state/resource comparison, policy denial, stale snapshot rejection, side-effect detection, and approval-aware shadow Gate
implementation.l2_evidence: 3 shadow contract tests plus eval_capability_shadow.py report gate.passed=true; read-only equivalence passes, side-effecting capability without approval is denied, and no shadow path executes side effects
implementation.l3_scope: atomic active-set commit, bounded resource reservation, resource exhaustion isolation, checkpoint persistence of resource ledger, replacement rollback, and disposer release audit
implementation.l3_evidence: 3 resource contract tests plus eval_capability_resource.py report gate.passed=true; resource exhaustion leaves snapshot and ledger unchanged, replacement rollback restores parent usage, and disposer release is recorded
implementation.l4_scope: independent admission review for pure-computation capability candidates; explicit value input, deterministic no-side-effect execution, independent oracle, and registry/policy/checkpoint compatibility
implementation.l4_evidence: review concludes no current workspace, IDE, terminal, MCP, or editor capability qualifies; implementation is No-Go and pseudo-pure executor admission is prohibited
implementation.next_stage: R5C-S0 long-horizon evidence window for structural growth

boundary: The registry owns capability lifecycle and safe dispatch; it does not own Taiji concepts, goals, memory, language, or learning.
Executors, MCP channels, permissions, policy, and side-effect rollback are not deletable knowledge artifacts and require their own lifecycle evidence.
R5B supplies reliable capability snapshots and outcomes to R5A/R5C but never mutates cognition directly.
dependencies: W7-R1 provider artifact binding for stale evidence
W7-R5A internalization must consume snapshots without owning them
W7-R5C structural growth may use registry outcomes only as evidence
replaces: registry and cognition sharing one owner

superseded_by.reason: R5B effector growth was absorbed into the Seed client plugin lifecycle and MCP client organ inheritance; body-side capability candidates are now owned by E5/E6 and admitted only through E-series Gates.
superseded_by.retained_value: seed_platform/capability_registry.py content-addressed bundles, snapshot/revision, disposer constraints and L4 no-go review remain valid prior evidence for E5/E6.
must_not_claim: This manifest no longer decides any current action.
Registry admission is not MCP client organ activation and does not grant connection authorization.
